item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Airways Men's National 7s halfback Terio Tamani will form the halves combination with fly-half Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula as new Flying Fijians coach Jake White looks to reignite the sleeping giant of Fiji Rugby when they face Japan in a Test match this Saturday.

White has named a formidable side to face the Brave Blossoms, with the assistance of his coaching staff, despite having spent only a short time with the team.

The Rugby World Cup-winning coach says players must earn their places in the team and work hard to wear the white jersey with pride.

White says he has spent just one week with the squad and is still getting to know the players.

However, he says the players have embraced everything introduced this week and there is no shortage of energy within the team.

White believes he can provide what Fiji Rugby needs and says the timing is right for him to take on the challenge of rebuilding the team and restoring its standing on the global stage.

He adds that there is plenty at stake this weekend as Fiji prepares to take on Japan's Brave Blossoms.

Fiji will play Japan at 5.50pm this Saturday in Tokyo.

Mitchell Moses ruled out of Rugby League World Cup after suffering leg injury
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/10/2026 The Kangaroos' Rugby League World Cup campaign has suffered a setback as halfback Mitchell Moses has been ruled out of the remainder of the tournament after suffering a leg injury against the Kiwis in the opening match last week.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/10/2026

The Kangaroos' Rugby League World Cup campaign has suffered a setback as halfback Mitchell Moses has been ruled out of the remainder of the tournament after suffering a leg injury against the Kiwis in the opening match last week.

The Kangaroos camp confirmed that the Parramatta playmaker had been diagnosed with a high-grade muscle tear following an MRI scan in Sydney.

Moses picked up the injury midway through the first half of Thursday night's game against the Kiwis and initially battled on after receiving treatment.

However, he lasted just two minutes into the second half before limping from the field.

Raiders five-eighth Ethan Strange will replace Moses in the 23-man Kangaroos squad in Brisbane.

Meanwhile, the Kangaroos will host the Vodafone Fiji Bati at 9.05pm on Sunday.

In other Round 2 matches, Tonga will face Lebanon at 9.05pm tomorrow, Papua New Guinea will meet Samoa at 4.25pm Saturday, while England will take on France at 6.35pm.

New Zealand will play the Cook Islands at 5.05pm on Sunday.

item.title: Semi Nabenu re-signs with Bula FC for 2027 season
item.description: Extra Bula FC midfielder Semi Nabenu returns for the 2027 OFC Professional League season, aiming to build on the experience gained during the club’s inaugural campaign. Son of former Fiji national footballer Waisea Nabenu, says he enjoyed his first season with the Warriors and wants to continue learning under Head Coach Stéphane Auvray.
item.content:encoded:
Extra Bula FC midfielder Semi Nabenu returns for the 2027 OFC Professional League season, aiming to build on the experience gained during the club’s inaugural campaign.

Son of former Fiji national footballer Waisea Nabenu, says he enjoyed his first season with the Warriors and wants to continue learning under Head Coach Stéphane Auvray.

He says representing a professional club from his home country is a privilege and an honour.

Nabenu says the team performed well in its first season, finishing third in the regular season before reaching the Top Four playoffs.

He says the experience helped him better understand his strengths and how he can contribute to the team, particularly in central midfield.

Nabenu says he also learned from experienced players, including captain Roy Krishna, Setareki Hughes and Gabriel Matanisiga, who helped him adapt to the professional environment.

He says Krishna has taught him valuable lessons, particularly about looking after his body and the importance of off-field preparation.

Nabenu’s football journey began in New Zealand, where he moved with his family in 2008 after his father received an opportunity to play football there.

He progressed through several clubs, including Otahuhu United, Central United, Bay Olympic and Onehunga Sports, before making his senior debut for Auckland United.

He later played for Birkenhead United and earned an opportunity with Auckland FC’s reserves in 2025.

Looking ahead to next season, Nabenu hopes to continue improving physically and technically, while also making an impact on the scoresheet.

He says the team can build on its first-season performance by having greater confidence and belief in its abilities.

Nabenu has also thanked the Bula Tribe for supporting the team during its inaugural season and is urging fans to continue backing the Warriors in 2027.

The 2027 OFC Pro League will begin in January next year.

Fiji Deaf Rugby 7s teams face funding and communication challenges ahead of World Cup
item.description: Despite facing financial and communication challenges, the Fiji's men's and women's Deaf Rugby Sevens teams are determined to make the country proud at the upcoming Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup in Japan. Head Coach Tevita Rokoqiqi, who has been coaching the teams since 2019, says the players have been in camp for almost a month and are ready to compete in the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Despite facing financial and communication challenges, the Fiji's men's and women's Deaf Rugby Sevens teams are determined to make the country proud at the upcoming Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup in Japan.

Head Coach Tevita Rokoqiqi, who has been coaching the teams since 2019, says the players have been in camp for almost a month and are ready to compete in the tournament.

Speaking to the media after the teams presented their traditional iTatau to Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru at the HFC Bank Stadium today, Rokoqiqi says funding remains one of their biggest challenges.

He says the teams have received $150,000 in government support through the Fiji Sports Commission, but more funding is needed to fully equip both the men's and women's teams.

Rokoqiqi also thanked the Fiji Rugby Union for donating rugby boots and the Australian Commission for providing clothing to the teams.

He says communication has also been a challenge, as he is not fluent in sign language and relies on interpreters to communicate with the players.

Despite these difficulties, Rokoqiqi says the teams are ready to compete and show what Deaf athletes can achieve.

He believes their participation will inspire children in the Deaf community to dream of representing Fiji one day.

Rokoqiqi recalls a recent visit to Gospel Primary School, where students were proud to meet former students who are now representing Fiji.

He is also calling for Deaf athletes to receive the same recognition and opportunities as other national representatives.

Meanwhile, Fiji's Youth Olympic team also presented its traditional iTatau to Saukuru at the HFC Bank Stadium today.

The Deaf Rugby Sevens teams and the Youth Olympic team are scheduled to depart Fiji next Monday.

The Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup will be held from the 31st of this month to the 3rd of November.

item.title: 17-year-old Maiwiriwiri excited to represent Fiji at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 17-year-old Anastasia Maiwiriwiri of Somosomo, Taveuni, says preparations for the upcoming Commonwealth Games are going well as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal. Student of Fiji Agape Mission School, Maiwiriwiri says she began playing basketball at the age of 13.
item.content:encoded:
17-year-old Anastasia Maiwiriwiri of Somosomo, Taveuni, says preparations for the upcoming Commonwealth Games are going well as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal.

Student of Fiji Agape Mission School, Maiwiriwiri says she began playing basketball at the age of 13.

She says her aunt and uncle encouraged her to take up the sport, and their support has played an important role in her basketball journey.

Maiwiriwiri says she is excited about the Commonwealth Games, with the team working well together during training sessions.

She says the sessions have been productive and enjoyable as the team prepares for the competition.

Maiwiriwiri who will be competing in the Basketball 3x3 has encouraged aspiring athletes to keep pushing forward, remain disciplined and continue believing in themselves.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.
